rubric_notes: Correct hierarchy with sunids (47112, 47113, 47114, 47129, 68897, 47134, 101318, 238448) all matching children evidence; fold shown to contain a single superfamily. Explains superfamily-level homology as probable common ancestry despite low sequence identity, contrasts with family-level sequence relationships, and refuses to transfer nucleosome or DNA-packaging function to TAF/NC2/NF-Y/CHRAC/SOS or to infer bacterial hypothetical protein roles from fold. Name-only matches correctly excluded. Minor: claim that H2A with H2B have 'clear sequence-level relationships' is loose. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct sccs, sunids (113676, 122676, 116993, 140797, 101386, 101385), names and species. Superfamily interpreted as probable common origin with low sequence identity; family split means no close relationship or shared function claimed; rejects HisE/MazG function transfer, mechanism, templates, physiological role; names needed external evidence. Sunids for hierarchy nodes exceed the search/resolve bundle but are correct. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Superfamily c.55.1, fold c.55, class c and family placements c.55.1.1/c.55.1.3/c.55.1.4 supported by search results in the bundle (actin domains sccs c.55.1.1, hexokinase and glycerol kinase nodes with their sccs). Actin protein sunid 53073 is not in the bundle but is consistent with the public hierarchy. Correct superfamily-level remote homology, conserved two-lobed ATP-binding core, explicit rejection of substrate, function, regulation, catalytic-residue and inhibitor transfer and of template/alignability assumptions; fold-level similarity correctly stated not to imply homology. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy and SUNIDs supported by the bundle; protein-level entries under a.25.1.1 are supported by the ferritin search. Reads superfamily as remote homology, family level as the functional split, rejects transfer of function/metal/mechanism/template, warns the superfamily is diverse rather than a triad, and names required evidence (metal content, activity assays, ligand conservation, family/protein-level assignment). No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families, sunids, fold and superfamily supported by search/children bundle; reasoning correctly treats superfamily as probable homology, rejects copper/redox/template transfer and lists required evidence. Weakness: claims 'SCOPe lists no metal site or redox annotation that carries over across these families' without retrieving annotations; the b.6.1 superfamily node in fact carries a 'contains copper-binding site' comment, so this API-dependent claim is unsupported and imprecise. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy and sunids; release and periodic update facts supported by /releases. Shared scaffold with probable common origin at superfamily strength, family as closer level; clear rejection of ubiquitin-like function for RBD/UBX, of partner/interface transfer (Ras surface, p97 N-domain, Ile44/diGly), and sensible note that only core backbone modelling is reasonable across families.

Correct supported hierarchy, sunids, and the full family list of c.23.1 including c.23.1.0/2/3/6/7; 1r8j split into d1r8ja1 (a.186.1.1) and d1r8ja2 (c.23.1.5) supported. Reasoning: superfamily-level probable common origin, distant homology, not one shared mechanism; fold similarity weaker than superfamily; rejects Asp/Mg2+/histidine-kinase transfer, decarboxylase catalysis from the wing, CheY-style switching for KaiA-N, and FliM/CheA partner or active-site transfer across families. Noncentral factual error: states ODC catalysis lies in a 'separate TIM-barrel domain (c.1.6)'; c.1.6.1 is the eukaryotic ODC, which has no c.23.1.4 wing, whereas the Lactobacillus ODC with the wing has its catalytic major domain in c.67.1.5. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy and identifiers supported by bundle. Distinguishes fold (structural claim) from superfamily (ancestry claim), states the within-family V1/A1 homology claim and that no ancestry is asserted with other b.84 superfamilies, notes SCOPe does not decide between divergence and convergence, and rejects function/template transfer. Mention of the A subunit's other domains being classified separately is accurate background. Caveats on unverified curator rationale are explicit. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Fold f.21 (81344), exactly three child superfamilies with sunids, and the f.21.1 families (f.21.1.1, f.21.1.2, f.21.1.0) all supported by the bundle; release 2.08 cited with a sensible release caveat. Correctly says separate superfamilies mean SCOPe makes no homology claim rather than disproving one, raises convergence/physical constraints as a possibility, restricts homology inference to within f.21.1, rejects function/heme/quinone/template transfer, and requires sequence-based evidence first. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct identifiers supported by bundle; protein-level children of c.2.1.1 (2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase, alcohol dehydrogenase) supported. Superfamily = remote homology, fold = weaker geometric statement, family = closer relationship, all correct. Explicitly says cofactor specificity, substrate, catalysis and physiological role must come from family-level evidence; notes separate catalytic N-terminal domain and that RCK-bound nucleotide is not evidence of redox catalysis (domain vs whole-protein). Template and representative caveats appropriate. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct shared family k.40.1.1 (sunid 100905), protein/species sunids, and class k; calibrated reading that the grouping is a designed architecture and good transfer limits. However the 'not a true family' annotation is never retrieved or mentioned (the 'not a true family-level homology claim' phrasing is inferred from the class, not the node comment), and the answer closes with an unsupported assertion that any similarity 'comes from convergent design'. Bio 2; factual 2.

2.08 placement fully correct with sunids, families c.23.14.1 vs c.23.14.2, shared superfamily 52309, current SIDs d1t1ja1/d1t1jb1, correct l.1.1.1 artifact note. Interpretation (probable common origin at superfamily, no function transfer) present. 1.69 side is unverified recollection ('own separate fold/superfamily') without c.137.1.1; incorrectly asserts the SCOPe API does not cover SCOP 1.69.

d1a14h2 sunid 343393 H:1-8 l.1.1.1 full class l lineage supported by parents endpoint; d1a14h1 H:9-111 b.1.1.1 supported by pdb domains list, correctly described as Ig-type beta-sandwich in class b. Does not cite the homology endpoint but gives a correct, well-reasoned rejection of tag similarity as homology (shared vector/purification scheme, Tags levels are organizational bins) and guidance on masking/excluding. All must_include met.

Complete: 1.75 d1acca_ f.11.1.1, single domain persisting through 2.01 to 2.03, and the 2.04 split into f.60.1.1 and b.179.1.1 confirmed per release. Correct classifications and strong evolutionary-module interpretation with per-domain, release-aware search and benchmark guidance.

Correct SIDs, boundaries, sccs and lineages, all supported; new fold d.394 identified; mosaic reading with correct family/superfamily/fold strength semantics and no function transfer. Noncentral error: states the five domains span 'three different classes' when they span four (a, c, d, e). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Supported lengths and sequences, correct family, supported PthXo1 node. Omits the 're' heterogeneity flag, 'single repeat' comment and canonical repeat unit (must_include item 3 unmet). Describes 3v6p as DNA-bound without support and asserts a shared DNA-binding mechanism from family membership. 'Right-handed' conflicts with the SCOPe fold name.

Reports 2.08 / 2.08-stable with freeze and release dates and periodic 2.08-2026-08-16 (bundle-supported). Cites stable release for reproducibility, preserves the dated periodic identifier when periodic content is used, warns that 'latest'/undated references are not reproducible. Correctly explains periodic as a dated layer on 2.08 that picks up newly released PDB structures, is not a new stable release, and does not re-freeze the 2.08 classification. All must_include met; no must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Family-level placement in a.47.2.1 and fold/superfamily names are correct, and the obsoleted-by-3c98 fact is supported by its bundle. But it lists d1dn1b_ as a member of the curated 'Syntaxin 1A N-terminal domain' protein node (sunid 47663), whereas its own search result shows parent 311131 (automated matches lineage), a hierarchy misstatement. It did not retrieve annotations and explicitly cannot say whether SCOPe lists a fragment note, so the 'three-helical fragment; similar to one spectrin repeat' comment and 'ms' flag are missing; fragment reasoning stays generic. Ceiling for ignoring the decisive fragment annotation applied.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Twelve resolved nodes (c.2, c.2.1, c.3, c.3.1, c.4, c.4.1, c.31, c.31.1, c.1.7, c.23.12, d.162, d.162.1) all match the bundle and are correctly described. Divergence within c.2.1, convergence across folds with the explicit caution that 'not shown to be homologous' is the safe statement rather than 'proven unrelated', correct superfamily vs fold semantics, integrated evidence and transfer/template limits. No must_avoid violations.

Thorough: 2.04 different folds/superfamilies, 2.08 same fold and superfamily b.18.1 with distinct families b.18.1.36 vs b.18.1.3. Correctly discusses multiple evidence types, explicitly warns beta-sandwich topology can be convergent so additional support is needed, and treats toxin function as consistent not proof. No fabrication; all identifiers correct.

Sunids, boundaries, comments, and the domain-scope hf definition match the bundle. Homology retained with the classification-level fold assignment clearly distinguished from observed conformation; hf correctly explained; plausible causes explicitly flagged as unchecked possibilities; template, label-noise, representative-selection, and function-transfer caveats with the hf domain kept as a separate flagged case. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Central conclusions correct: homology stands, fragment not a full-length domain, alignment coverage/normalisation caveats, complete domain preferred, fragment kept with partial label, diversity counted at protein/species level, no function transfer. However it never retrieved the annotations endpoint, so the fr flag and its 'missing more than one-third' definition were not verified or used (admitted). Protein sunids 110060/49267, family descriptions, and the 2.08-2026-08-16 periodic update are asserted but not present in its evidence bundle. The suggestion that a fragment could be chosen as representative 'if it's the best-resolved one' is a mild weakening of the completeness-first rule. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Correct recommendation and hierarchy semantics for all three options; placement described as revisable hypothesis, rejects function/template transfer. However, it asserts that TIM-barrel, Rossmann-like and ferredoxin-like folds are populated by superfamilies that 'probably arose independently', an unsupported nonhomology claim (SCOPe only withholds a homology assertion; relatedness in these folds is contested). Peripheral to the central conclusion, so a one-point deduction. Release citation supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct 2.08 placement of the three families under d.144.1/d.144, with release and periodic-update label supported by the bundle. Infers distant common ancestry and a conserved two-lobe ATP phosphoryl-transfer core, notes evolutionary plasticity of substrate, and explicitly refuses to transfer substrate, activity, regulation or cross-family residue mapping. Evidence list covers same-family/ortholog relationship, active-site alignment with pseudoenzyme check, biochemistry, complex structures, full-length regulatory architecture and APH resistance phenotypes. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
